edition: Latin–English column of the Saints.Bible Parallel Reader
source_latin: Clementine Vulgate (Vulgata Clementina), as displayed on the Saints.Bible staging comparison pages

verses.latin: Paulus , et Silvanus, et Timotheus ecclesiæ Thessalonicensium in Deo Patre, et Domino Jesu Christo.
verses.english: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Gratia vobis, et pax. Gratias agimus Deo semper pro omnibus vobis, memoriam vestri facientes in orationibus nostris sine intermissione,
verses.english: Grace to you and peace. We always give thanks to God for you all, making mention of you in our prayers without ceasing,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: memores operis fidei vestræ, et laboris, et caritatis, et sustinentiæ spei Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ante Deum et Patrem nostrum:
verses.english: remembering the work of your faith, your labor and love, and the endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: scientes, fratres dilecti a Deo, electionem vestram:
verses.english: We know, brothers beloved by God, that he has chosen you,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: quia Evangelium nostrum non fuit ad vos in sermone tantum, sed et in virtute, et in Spiritu Sancto, et in plenitudine multa, sicut scitis quales fuerimus in vobis propter vos.
verses.english: for our gospel came to you not in word alone, but also in power, in the Holy Spirit, and in great fullness. You know what kind of people we were among you for your sake.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Et vos imitatores nostri facti estis, et Domini, excipientes verbum in tribulatione multa, cum gaudio Spiritus Sancti:
verses.english: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in great tribulation with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: ita ut facti sitis forma omnibus credentibus in Macedonia, et in Achaia.
verses.english: so that you became an example to all who believe in Macedonia and Achaia.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: A vobis enim diffamatus est sermo Domini, non solum in Macedonia, et in Achaia, sed et in omni loco fides vestra, quæ est ad Deum, profecta est ita ut non sit nobis necesse quidquam loqui.
verses.english: For the word of the Lord has spread abroad from you, not in Macedonia and Achaia alone. In every place your faith toward God has gone forth, so that we need say nothing.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Ipsi enim de nobis annuntiant qualem introitum habuerimus ad vos: et quomodo conversi estis ad Deum a simulacris, servire Deo vivo, et vero,
verses.english: For they themselves tell how we came among you and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: et exspectare Filium ejus de cælis (quem suscitavit a mortuis) Jesum, qui eripuit nos ab ira ventura.
verses.english: and to wait for his Son from heaven, Jesus, whom he raised from the dead and who has delivered us from the wrath to come.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Nam ipsi scitis, fratres, introitum nostrum ad vos, quia non inanis fuit:
verses.english: For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: sed ante passi, et contumeliis affecti (sicut scitis) in Philippis, fiduciam habuimus in Deo nostro, loqui ad vos Evangelium Dei in multa sollicitudine.
verses.english: But after we had suffered and been shamefully mistreated at Philippi, as you know, we had confidence in our God to speak the gospel of God to you amid great distress.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Exhortatio enim nostra non de errore, neque de immunditia, neque in dolo,
verses.english: For our exhortation comes neither from error nor from impurity, nor is it made in deceit.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: sed sicut probati sumus a Deo ut crederetur nobis Evangelium: ita loquimur non quasi hominibus placentes, sed Deo, qui probat corda nostra.
verses.english: Just as God approved us to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak to please God, who tests our hearts, rather than people.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Neque enim aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis, sicut scitis: neque in occasione avaritiæ: Deus testis est:
verses.english: For we never spoke with flattery, as you know, nor did we use a pretext for greed. God is witness.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: nec quærentes ab hominibus gloriam, neque a vobis, neque ab aliis.
verses.english: Nor did we seek glory from people, whether from you or from others.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Cum possemus vobis oneri esse ut Christi apostoli: sed facti sumus parvuli in medio vestrum, tamquam si nutrix foveat filios suos.
verses.english: Though we could have been a burden to you as apostles of Christ, we became little children among you, as a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Ita desiderantes vos, cupide volebamus tradere vobis non solum Evangelium Dei, sed etiam animas nostras: quoniam carissimi nobis facti estis.
verses.english: So deeply did we long for you that we were eager to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own souls as well, because you had become so dear to us.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Memores enim estis, fratres, laboris nostri, et fatigationis: nocte ac die operantes, ne quem vestrum gravaremus, prædicavimus in vobis Evangelium Dei.
verses.english: For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil. Working night and day so as to be a burden to none of you, we preached the gospel of God among you.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Vos testes estis, et Deus, quam sancte, et juste, et sine querela, vobis, qui credidistis, fuimus:
verses.english: You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy and just and blameless our conduct was toward you who believed.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: sicut scitis, qualiter unumquemque vestrum (sicut pater filios suos)
verses.english: You know how we dealt with each of you as a father with his own children,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: deprecantes vos, et consolantes, testificati sumus, ut ambularetis digne Deo, qui vocavit vos in suum regnum et gloriam.
verses.english: pleading with you, comforting you, and bearing witness that you should walk in a manner worthy of God, who called you into his kingdom and glory.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Ideo et nos gratias agimus Deo sine intermissione: quoniam cum accepissetis a nobis verbum auditus Dei, accepistis illud, non ut verbum hominum, sed (sicut est vere) verbum Dei, qui operatur in vobis, qui credidistis:
verses.english: Therefore we also give thanks to God without ceasing, because when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it as it truly is, the word of God rather than the word of men. God is at work in you who have believed.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: vos enim imitatores facti estis, fratres, ecclesiarum Dei, quæ sunt in Judæa in Christo Jesu: quia eadem passi estis et vos a contribulibus vestris, sicut et ipsi a Judæis:
verses.english: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Christ Jesus that are in Judea. You suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: qui et Dominum occiderunt Jesum, et prophetas, et nos persecuti sunt, et Deo non placent, et omnibus hominibus adversantur,
verses.english: who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us. They displease God and oppose everyone,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: prohibentes nos gentibus loqui ut salvæ fiant, ut impleant peccata sua semper: pervenit enim ira Dei super illos usque in finem.
verses.english: preventing us from speaking to the Gentiles that they might be saved. Thus they are always filling up their sins, for the wrath of God has come upon them to the end.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Nos autem fratres desolati a vobis ad tempus horæ, aspectu, non corde, abundantius festinavimus faciem vestram videre cum multo desiderio:
verses.english: But as for us, brothers, when we were bereft of you for a short time, in sight though not in heart, we hastened all the more to see your face, with great longing.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: quoniam voluimus venire ad vos, ego quidem Paulus, et semel, et iterum: sed impedivit nos Satanas.
verses.english: For we wanted to come to you. I, Paul, wanted to come once and again, but Satan hindered us.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Quæ est enim nostra spes aut gaudium, aut corona gloriæ? nonne vos ante Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum estis in adventu ejus?
verses.english: For what is our hope or joy or crown of glory? Is it not you before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: vos enim estis gloria nostra et gaudium.
verses.english: For you are our glory and joy.
verses.english_origin: Douay-Rheims (Challoner), verbatim
verses.translation_review: Modernized English scaffold · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Propter quod non sustinentes amplius, placuit nobis remanere Athenis, solis:
verses.english: Therefore, when we could bear it no longer, we decided to remain at Athens alone,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: et misimus Timotheum fratrem nostrum, et ministrum Dei in Evangelio Christi, ad confirmandos vos, et exhortandos pro fide vestra:
verses.english: and we sent Timothy, our brother and God’s minister in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you in your faith,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: ut nemo moveatur in tribulationibus istis: ipsi enim scitis quod in hoc positi sumus.
verses.english: so that no one should be shaken by these tribulations. You yourselves know that we are appointed for this.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Nam et cum apud vos essemus, prædicebamus vobis passuros nos tribulationes, sicut et factum est, et scitis.
verses.english: For even when we were with you, we kept telling you beforehand that we would suffer tribulations. And so it happened, as you know.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Propterea et ego amplius non sustinens, misi ad cognoscendam fidem vestram: ne forte tentaverit vos is qui tentat, et inanis fiat labor noster.
verses.english: For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I too sent to learn about your faith, for fear that the tempter might have tempted you and our labor might come to nothing.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Nunc autem veniente Timotheo ad nos a vobis, et annuntiante nobis fidem et caritatem vestram, et quia memoriam nostri habetis bonam semper, desiderantes nos videre, sicut et nos quoque vos:
verses.english: But now Timothy has come to us from you and brought word of your faith and love. He told us that you always remember us kindly and long to see us as we long to see you.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: ideo consolati sumus, fratres, in vobis in omni necessitate et tribulatione nostra, per fidem vestram,
verses.english: For this reason, brothers, through your faith we were comforted concerning you in all our need and tribulation,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: quoniam nunc vivimus, si vos statis in Domino.
verses.english: for now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Quam enim gratiarum actionem possumus Deo retribuere pro vobis in omni gaudio, quo gaudemus propter vos ante Deum nostrum,
verses.english: For what thanks can we return to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice on your account before our God,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: nocte ac die abundantius orantes, ut videamus faciem vestram, et compleamus ea quæ desunt fidei vestræ?
verses.english: as night and day we pray ever more earnestly to see your face and supply what is lacking in your faith?
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Ipse autem Deus, et Pater noster, et Dominus noster Jesus Christus, dirigat viam nostram ad vos.
verses.english: Now may our God and Father himself and our Lord Jesus Christ direct our way to you.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Vos autem Dominus multiplicet, et abundare faciat caritatem vestram in invicem, et in omnes, quemadmodum et nos in vobis:
verses.english: And may the Lord cause you to increase and make your love abound toward one another and toward all, as ours abounds toward you,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: ad confirmanda corda vestra sine querela in sanctitate, ante Deum et Patrem nostrum, in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum omnibus sanctis ejus. Amen.
verses.english: to strengthen your hearts so that they are blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. Amen.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: De cetero ergo, fratres, rogamus vos et obsecramus in Domino Jesu, ut quemadmodum accepistis a nobis quomodo oporteat vos ambulare, et placere Deo, sic et ambuletis ut abundetis magis.
verses.english: Finally, brothers, we ask and implore you in the Lord Jesus to walk in the way you learned from us, the way you ought to walk and please God, so that you may abound still more.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Scitis enim quæ præcepta dederim vobis per Dominum Jesum.
verses.english: For you know what commands I gave you through the Lord Jesus.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Hæc est enim voluntas Dei, sanctificatio vestra: ut abstineatis vos a fornicatione,
verses.english: For this is the will of God, your sanctification, that you abstain from fornication,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: ut sciat unusquisque vestrum vas suum possidere in sanctificatione, et honore:
verses.english: that each of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: non in passione desiderii, sicut et gentes, quæ ignorant Deum:
verses.english: not in the passion of lust like the Gentiles who do not know God,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: et ne quis supergrediatur, neque circumveniat in negotio fratrem suum: quoniam vindex est Dominus de his omnibus, sicut prædiximus vobis, et testificati sumus.
verses.english: and that no one overstep or take advantage of his brother in the matter, for the Lord is the avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly testified.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Non enim vocavit nos Deus in immunditiam, sed in sanctificationem.
verses.english: For God did not call us to impurity, but to sanctification.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Itaque qui hæc spernit, non hominem spernit, sed Deum: qui etiam dedit Spiritum suum Sanctum in nobis.
verses.english: Therefore whoever rejects these things rejects not man, but God, who has also given his Holy Spirit within us.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: De caritate autem fraternitatis non necesse habemus scribere vobis: ipsi enim vos a Deo didicistis ut diligatis invicem.
verses.english: Now concerning brotherly love, we have no need to write to you, for you yourselves have learned from God to love one another.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Etenim illud facitis in omnes fratres in universa Macedonia. Rogamus autem vos, fratres, ut abundetis magis,
verses.english: And indeed you do this toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to abound still more,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: et operam detis ut quieti sitis, et ut vestrum negotium agatis, et operemini manibus vestris, sicut præcepimus vobis:
verses.english: and to make it your aim to live quietly, attend to your own affairs, and work with your hands, as we commanded you,
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: et ut honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt: et nullius aliquid desideretis.
verses.english: so that you may walk honorably toward outsiders and not desire anything that belongs to another.
verses.english_origin: Saints.Bible editorial revision from the Clementine Vulgate
verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.latin: Nolumus autem vos ignorare fratres de dormientibus, ut non contristemini sicut et ceteri, qui spem non habent.
verses.english: Now, brothers, we do not want you to be ignorant about those who sleep, so that you may not grieve as the others do who have no hope.

verses.translation_review: Latin–English editorial revision · checked against the Clementine Latin (7 November 2026) · specialist sign-off pending

verses.english: For we say this to you by the word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the Lord’s coming, will not precede those who have fallen asleep.

verses.english: For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel and the trumpet of God, and the dead who are in Christ will rise first.
